items.claim: The onset warrant turns on an unquoted Hebrew shape-parallel that the bytes show is a different construction, and the ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: The opening splice reaches byte tier and the construction is byte-true: רְא֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier). But the seam warrant, and the rejected alternative that leans on it, assert sameness of shape with web:Jer.2.4 without ever quoting that verse in the original-language witness or citing it under an oshb: ref; the bytes there read שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier), a different imperative. Named as objects and swept separately, they are not one shape: the hear-construction stands at 10 verses (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier) while the see-construction stands at 1 verse, this one (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier). Second, the span covers one ketiv/qere note, at oshb:Jer.2.33, and the entry lacks any ketiv/qere disclosure, though that verse is argued in prose as the seeking-love charge; the note is a person alternation, unpointed למדתי standing beside pointed לִמַּ֖דְתְּ (oshb:Jer.2.33, byte tier), and “you have even taught” (web:Jer.2.33) renders the pointed form. Third, the rear-seam statement that the inventories carry nothing further before the next unit's topic shift leaves a byte-true device crossing that seam undisclosed: שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ (oshb:Jer.2.35, byte tier), rendered “his anger has turned away from me” (web:Jer.2.35), carries the return root two verses before this unit's close, on a seam whose next unit is built on that root, and the anger-turning idiom stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier), the other at oshb:Jer.4.8. Verified as written: no petuchah or setumah falls anywhere in 2:30-2:37 (tier-3, single witness), so the marks-silence sentence is correct and the absence is rightly not read as counterevidence.

items.claim: A plene-bound substring digit is presented as a root count and carries a book-wide priority claim the bytes refute, while the onset argument leaves the verse's opening word and its closing formula unengaged.
items.evidence: The cited digit reproduces exactly for the contiguous consonantal run of the plene spelling (sweep: 41 verses, skeleton tier, earliest at Jer.3.1), but the sentence carrying it names the swept object as the return root. That needle is spelling-bound and misses defective writings of the root, so the root stands earlier at least twice: וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.19, byte tier), rendered “your backsliding will rebuke you” (web:Jer.2.19), and שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ (oshb:Jer.2.35, byte tier), rendered “his anger has turned away from me” (web:Jer.2.35) - both witnesses carry the root before this onset, so the earliest-in-the-book claim is false at the level it is asserted, and naming the tier does not dampen an exclusivity claim. Second, the onset is argued as opening with no formula of its own, but the verse's first word is לֵאמֹ֡ר (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier), a bound speech-frame infinitive with no governing verb of speaking anywhere in the verse - a byte-true frame element sitting exactly at the seam and arguing dependence on what precedes rather than a fresh start; and the same verse closes נְאֻם יְהֹוָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier), a closure formula at the end of the span's opening verse. Neither is engaged. Third, three of the span's five verses carry ketiv/qere notes (oshb:Jer.3.2, oshb:Jer.3.4, oshb:Jer.3.5) and none is disclosed, although the parashah inventory was plainly read at Jer.3.5, where the petuchah citation is correct as to type and verse (tier-3, single witness). Fourth, the stated extent of the wordplay cluster is contested by the same root: the anger-turning idiom stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier), oshb:Jer.2.35 and oshb:Jer.4.8 - כִּ֥י לֹא שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ (oshb:Jer.4.8, byte tier) - one on each side of the claimed cluster, both outside it.

items.claim: The declared disposition on the missing ketiv/qere disclosure is refuted: the note at Jer.3.7 is live, sits in the clause quoted in prose, and carries the reading both witnesses render.
items.evidence: Everything structural verifies. The opening splice reaches byte tier; the two petuchah citations are the correct type at the correct verses, Jer.3.5 and Jer.3.10, and do bracket the span exactly (tier-3, single witness); the backsliding noun does stand at both cited verses and the book-wide object is 5 verses (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier: 3:6, 3:8, 3:11, 3:12, 8:5); and the speech-introduction verb does recur in full at oshb:Jer.3.11 rather than carrying over. The disclosure gap, however, is a real defect rather than a heuristic artifact: the span covers a ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.3.7 and no field mentions it, while the note stands immediately before the clause quoted in prose - unpointed ותראה beside pointed וַתֵּ֛רֶא, then בָּגוֹדָ֥ה אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.7, byte tier) - and “her treacherous sister Judah saw it” (web:Jer.3.7) renders the pointed form. Leaving it out leaves the book's variant inventory (141 notes over 124 verses) unmarked at a verse the argument relies on. Secondary and lower-weight: the reign anchor is byte-true, בִּימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.3.6, byte tier), but filing it under a date-frame signal key overstates it, since this construction is not the year-formula shape and the book's byte-derived date-header candidate list does not carry this site.

items.claim: The one-unit warrant rests on a blanket no-imperative and no-addressee-shift statement that the pointed bytes contradict twice inside the span, and the doubled ketiv/qere at the very verse the rejected rival turns on is undisclosed.
items.evidence: Both splices reach byte tier, and the parashah citations are right: setumah inside the span at Jer.3.17 and petuchah immediately before it at Jer.3.10, each named under its own type (tier-3, single witness); the backsliding noun does recur at the two cited verses. The load-bearing claim fails on the bytes. Inside the span, אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier) is a fresh feminine-singular imperative, and שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) is a fresh plural imperative with a fresh plural vocative - a number shift away from the singular addressee of שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier). Both witnesses carry the shift: “Return, you backsliding Israel,” (web:Jer.3.12) against “Return, backsliding children,” (web:Jer.3.14). So a fresh imperative and a fresh addressee do fall between the invitation and the promise material the unit keeps with it. The rejected rival at Jer.3.19 is raised and dismissed on a translation-side ground - that the English opens a fresh quotation there - while the Hebrew pivot at that verse, וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier), an emphatic independent pronoun before the perfect, is left unquoted and unweighed. That same verse carries two ketiv/qere notes, both undisclosed, and both are second-person number alternations bearing directly on the addressee question the unit gets wrong: unpointed תקראו beside pointed תִּקְרְאִי, and unpointed תשובו beside pointed תָשֽׁוּבִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier), the second riding on the return root the unit is built around. Finally, splice and gloss extents part company at oshb:Jer.3.12: the Hebrew stops at נְאֻם while the rendering set beside it runs to the end of the verse.

items.claim: The renewed-call claim is unanchored and untiered: the call is a two-site refrain whose other member sits in the immediately preceding block, so a byte-true device straddles this front seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: Both splices reach byte tier; the setumah citation is the correct type at Jer.3.25, the marks inventory really is silent across 3:21-3:24 and at the front seam (tier-3, single witness), and no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in 3:21-3:25, so nothing is owed there. But שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) is not a fresh call. The same three-word run stands at exactly one other verse in the book (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier): שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) - identical to it at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier, the noun's dagesh and the accents differing. Calling it renewed without naming the prior site or the tier leaves a byte-true refrain straddling this front seam undisclosed, and that refrain argues continuity with the material the seam is meant to separate. A second hook crosses the same seam in a second spelling object: the bare-heights noun here is the plene שְׁפָיִ֣ים (oshb:Jer.3.21, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, the other at Jer.4.11), while the same imagery earlier in this chapter is the defective שְׁפָיִ֜ם (oshb:Jer.3.2, byte tier; sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier) - one English gloss, two attested spellings, neither named.

items.claim: The voice-turn seam, both mark citations, and the disclosed cross-seam root continuity verify against the bytes and the inventories.
items.evidence: The splice reaches byte tier and covers the whole verse. The warrant is byte-true: the divine formula stands inside the conditional, נְאֻם יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Jer.4.1, byte tier), with the addressee named, יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל (oshb:Jer.4.1, byte tier), against the first-person-plural confession that precedes it, כִּי֩ לַיהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ חָטָ֗אנוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.3.25, byte tier) - a speaker turn, not merely a topic turn. Both setumah citations are the correct type at the correct verses, Jer.3.25 immediately before the span and Jer.4.2 at its close (tier-3, single witness), and no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in 4:1-4:2, so no variant disclosure is owed. The return-root continuity across the front seam is disclosed rather than suppressed, and the two forms are actually present, אִם תָּשׁ֨וּב and אֵלַ֖י תָּשׁ֑וּב (oshb:Jer.4.1, byte tier). Noted without defeating the unit: the splice runs the full verse while the rendering beside it stops at the opening clause, leaving the abomination clause unglossed; and the recurrence is stated at root level without a per-form count naming the form.

items.claim: The speech-formula onset, its frame owner, the addressee narrowing, and the mark statements verify at byte tier, and the conjunction-prefixed formula shape is the book's ordinary onset form rather than a weakened one.
items.evidence: The splice reaches byte tier and the formula is byte-true at the head of the verse: כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.4.3, byte tier). The frame owner is named and is correct - the formula stands in the divine mouth here, not inside quoted human speech, which is the live hazard elsewhere in this book. The conjunction prefix does not weaken the onset: verse-initial instances of this conjunction-prefixed formula stand at 28 verses (sweep: 28 verses, skeleton tier) beside 62 verse-initial bare-formula instances (sweep: 62 verses, skeleton tier), so the shape is a normal onset form. The addressee narrowing is byte-true, לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.4.3, byte tier) against יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל (oshb:Jer.4.1, byte tier). The mark statements verify exactly: setumah at Jer.4.2 immediately before the span, and no petuchah or setumah anywhere in 4:3-4:4 (tier-3, single witness), with the absence correctly not read as counterevidence; no ketiv/qere note falls in the span; and gloss and splice extents agree. Noted without defeating the unit: the forward reference to the following verse pairs the opening imperative with the third rather than with the adjacent second, and that verse is characterised in prose without appearing among the boundary evidence refs.

items.claim: The no-address-shift claim that carries the rejected internal cut and the high confidence is contested by the Hebrew: the second-person forms change number at the very verse where the entry denies any shift, and the speaking voice changes with them.
items.evidence: The strong parts verify first: all three splices reach byte tier; the variant note at oshb:Jer.4.5 is disclosed and handled correctly, with the pointed form quoted - unpointed ותקעו standing beside pointed תִּקְע֥וּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier); the petuchah inside the span at Jer.4.8 is the correct type and is correctly held non-driving (tier-3, single witness); and the divine formula does stand at oshb:Jer.4.9. The contested claim is the parenthesis denying any address or formula shift at Jer.4.7. The summons commands a plural through the two preceding verses - הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier) and שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס צִיּ֔וֹנָה הָעִ֖יזוּ אַֽל תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) - while Jer.4.7 turns to singular possessive suffixes, אַרְצֵךְ֙ and עָרַ֥יִךְ (oshb:Jer.4.7, byte tier); the number change is consonantally certain (a singular final-kaf suffix where a plural addressee would be written with mem), and the pointing reads the suffixes feminine. The rendering “to make your land desolate, that your cities be laid waste” (web:Jer.4.7) is number-blind and cannot register the change, so the denial holds on the translation side but not in the Hebrew. The speaking voice moves with it: divine first person at כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִצָּפ֖וֹן (oshb:Jer.4.6, byte tier) gives way to third-person description, then to a first-person-plural speaker who refers to Yahweh in the third person, כִּ֥י לֹא שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ (oshb:Jer.4.8, byte tier), before the divine formula returns at Jer.4.9. The rejected alternative dismisses a cut at Jer.4.7 for lacking an imperative, vocative or speech formula without weighing any of this, and the unit is held at high confidence on that basis. Smaller and separate: the variant note is described as sitting on the verb that opens this unit's imperative, but it sits on the verse's third imperative, not on the opening הַגִּ֣ידוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier).
